assessment.cross_component_synthesis: On March 21, the available signals describe a population that continues to seek physical protection under missile fire while confronting infrastructure deficits that undermine that protection. A kindergarten struck in Beit Shemesh has prompted school closures and public acknowledgment that kindergartens in the area lack shelters entirely — a gap reported by community advocates alongside calls for a local medical center. The dominant public narrative remains one of disrupted normalcy rather than effective coping: residents are described as living 'in limbo,' a 70-year-old was injured running to a protected space, and a shelter assault in Petah Tikva indicates that physical co-location under stress is generating interpersonal conflict rather than solidarity. Leadership visibility is present at the incident level — the deputy mayor arrived at the kindergarten strike site — but there is no evidence of coordinated community resource mobilization, structured communication to residents, or organized support for at-risk groups on this date.
assessment.evidence_quality_note: The available signals for March 21 are limited to six distinct source articles, with most behavioral evidence drawn from official statements and reported incidents rather than direct resident testimony, reducing confidence in population-wide generalizations.

manifestations_evidenced: Competing or contradictory narratives are explicitly voiced by residents or groups
manifestations_absent: A narrative of successful coping is visible and circulating
The coping story reflects the entire population, not just a subset
Residents express that the authority's narrative is credible and reflects their lived reality
evidence: Deputy mayor Avi Hayim said: 'It's lucky there are no children here. A great disaster could have happened' — framing the event in terms of near-miss rather than managed response ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx))
A 70-year-old resident was injured while running to a protected space during the missile barrage, reflecting the physical cost of continued exposure ([source](https://news.walla.co.il/break/3825251))

A Petah Tikva resident in his 20s was arrested on suspicion of attacking his neighbor in a shelter during an air raid siren, after the neighbor made a remark ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/men-men_news/Article-4efeb1817bd0d91026.htm))

Article framing describes Beit Shemesh residents as 'learning to live in limbo' after a direct hit caused extensive destruction and fatalities ([source](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-890471))
components.narrative: The public narrative in evidence on March 21 centers on disruption, near-miss, and uncertainty rather than managed resilience. Officials describe a struck kindergarten in terms of what could have happened rather than what was prevented, and residents in Beit Shemesh are characterized as 'living in limbo' following direct strike damage ([source](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-890471)). No evidence is present of an official or community-led narrative framing the situation as one of effective collective coping. This continues the declining trajectory observed in prior days, where residents have voiced exhaustion and a sense that conditions are not improving. The signals available reflect a predominantly negative narrative environment, with no countering positive-coping story surfacing in the data on this date.

manifestations_absent: Residents state they receive the information they need to function during the emergency
Authority communication mechanisms are adapted to different resident groups (language, channel, format)
Residents express trust in information received from the authority
Population perceives national media information as relevant and addressing their needs

components.narrative: No signals pertaining to information or communication were extracted for March 21, leaving this component without behavioral evidence for the current date. It is not possible to characterize whether residents received functional guidance, whether communication channels were operational, or whether gaps in information were being experienced. This absence of signal does not indicate that communication was functioning well — it reflects a data gap. Given the prior recorded score of 2/10 on March 19, and no indication of structural improvement in the intervening period, the component remains a concern. Assessment of this dimension will require additional sourcing.

manifestations_evidenced: Residents express or demonstrate perception of the situation as genuinely life-threatening
manifestations_absent: Community teams or roles actively promote emergency preparedness among residents
Residents or officials report non-compliance with protective guidelines
evidence: A 70-year-old resident was injured while running to a protected space during the missile barrage, indicating movement toward shelter in response to warning ([source](https://news.walla.co.il/break/3825251))
components.narrative: The single behavioral signal for this component on March 21 is an elderly resident who was injured while running to a protected space during a missile barrage. This indicates that residents are responding to sirens by attempting to reach shelter, consistent with Home Front Command guidance. However, the injury itself reflects a differential functioning split: the protective behavior is occurring, but physical conditions — including the absence of shelters in some locations — mean that compliance does not guarantee safety. No evidence is present of community-led preparedness promotion or structured guidance reinforcement. The signal base for this component remains limited, and the prior-day score of 8/10 should be interpreted with caution given the infrastructure gaps surfacing in adjacent components.

manifestations_evidenced: Schools and educational institutions are open and operating (or explicitly closed/disrupted)
Specific disruptions to daily life are reported (closures, evacuations, inability to work)
manifestations_absent: Residents succeed in managing daily life (reported continuation of work, commerce, or social roles)
Residents report that sufficient resources are available to maintain routine functioning
Essential services (healthcare, supply chains, municipal services) continue to operate
evidence: Mayor Raz Kinstlich stated: 'You see what happened here, complete damage to the kindergarten. We will not open the education system until...' — indicating a closure decision following the strike ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx))

Anbor Bloch states: 'We discovered there are no shelters at all in kindergartens' and emphasizes the need for a medical center in the area ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/Article-1298570))
components.narrative: Functional continuity on March 21 is demonstrably disrupted in the education sector, with the mayor of the affected municipality announcing that the education system will not reopen following the kindergarten strike ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx)). A split is evident between the disruption that has occurred and the infrastructure gap that preceded it: a community advocate reports that kindergartens in the area had no shelters at all, meaning the continuity failure was partly foreseeable ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/Article-1298570)). No signals indicate that other essential services — healthcare, commerce, or municipal operations — are functioning or disrupted, reflecting a data gap rather than confirmed continuity. The absence of medical facilities in the area, as described by the same advocate, suggests that healthcare continuity is also a concern. The component's prior score of 1/10 is consistent with the evidence present today.

manifestations_absent: Residents volunteer or express willingness to volunteer in formal or informal frameworks
Authority or organizations are observed to activate and coordinate community resources
Mechanisms exist and operate to coordinate volunteers and community organizations
Cross-sector cooperation (e.g., municipality + NGOs + businesses) is reported or observed
evidence: Anbor Bloch, described as a prominent voice on northern border hardship, publicly advocates for a medical center and identifies the absence of shelters in kindergartens — an example of civil society actors surfacing unmet needs ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/Article-1298570))
components.narrative: The signal available for community capital on March 21 reflects advocacy rather than mobilization: a civil society figure is publicly naming infrastructure deficits rather than coordinating resources to address them. No evidence is present of volunteer activation, cross-sector cooperation, or formal community resource coordination. A differential is visible between the presence of engaged community voices and the absence of institutional mechanisms through which those voices translate into organized action. This is consistent with the prior-day score of 10/10, which reflected strong community capital — however, today's evidence does not confirm that this capital is being actively deployed in organized frameworks, warranting closer observation.

manifestations_evidenced: Leadership is reported to function professionally and manage the situation competently
manifestations_absent: Residents express that formal or informal leadership is a source of support and security
Leadership actively encourages residents to follow HFC guidelines

evidence: Deputy mayor Avi Hayim arrived at the scene of the kindergarten strike and made a public statement ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx))
Mayor Raz Kinstlich was present at the scene and issued a statement regarding educational closures ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx))
components.narrative: Municipal leadership demonstrated physical presence at the site of the kindergarten strike on March 21, with both the deputy mayor and the mayor making public statements from the location. This represents visible incident-level leadership response. However, the statements recorded describe the damage and announce a closure decision rather than providing operational guidance to residents or publicly reinforcing protective behavior. No evidence is present of residents characterizing leadership as a source of support or security, and no evidence of resident criticism of leadership appears in today's signals. The behavioral record for leadership on this date is narrow — physical presence at one incident — and does not allow for assessment of broader leadership functioning across the affected population.

manifestations_evidenced: Population groups are reported as scapegoated, blamed, or excluded due to the emergency (negative signal)
manifestations_absent: Residents express a sense of solidarity or shared fate (in their own words)
Concrete acts of mutual aid between residents are reported
Programs or events strengthening belonging are activated and attended
evidence: A Petah Tikva resident in his 20s was arrested on suspicion of attacking his neighbor in a shelter during an air raid siren; the neighbor had made a remark, and in response the suspect headbutted him in the face, causing injuries requiring medical treatment ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/men-men_news/Article-4efeb1817bd0d91026.htm))
components.narrative: The sole behavioral signal for belonging and solidarity on March 21 is a reported interpersonal assault occurring within a shared shelter space during an air raid siren in Petah Tikva. The incident — in which a remark prompted a physical attack between neighbors — illustrates the interpersonal stress that can emerge when residents are confined together under sustained pressure. No evidence of mutual aid, solidarity expressions, or community-building activity was recorded on this date. The component's prior-day score of 7/10 reflected stronger belonging indicators; today's signal base is insufficient to confirm whether that baseline holds or has deteriorated, though the absence of positive signals and the presence of a conflict incident indicate ongoing fragility.

Deputy mayor Avi Hayim said: 'It's lucky there are no children here. A great disaster could have happened' — indicating children were absent from the struck kindergarten at the time ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx))
Mayor Raz Kinstlich indicated the education system will not reopen following the kindergarten strike ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rkz5ttj9bx))
Anbor Bloch states: 'We discovered there are no shelters at all in kindergartens' and calls for a medical center in the area ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/Article-1298570))
A shelter assault in Petah Tikva resulted in injuries requiring medical treatment, involving a resident in his 20s ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/men-women_news/Article-4efeb1817bd0d91026.htm))
components.narrative: Wellbeing indicators for at-risk populations on March 21 reflect a pattern of unmet physical safety needs rather than organized response. A differential is visible between two populations: elderly residents face physical injury risk when running to inadequate or distant shelter, while young children's exposure is being managed through school closures rather than provision of safe spaces. The absence of shelters in kindergartens — reported publicly only now, following a strike — indicates that the infrastructure gap preceded the event and was not proactively addressed ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/Article-1298570)). No evidence is present of mental health services being deployed or of organized outreach to at-risk groups on this date. The shelter assault in Petah Tikva adds a secondary wellbeing concern: physical harm arising within protection spaces rather than outside them.
